query: A Name to Call The first appointment is under the open dome, past midnight. Your tutor says a star's name aloud, the old name, the one on no chart, and points. "Ask it for a thread of its light," the tutor says. "Ask properly. It has been asked rudely before." Call until it answers You call until your voice goes and your hands are numb on the rail. At four the thread comes down, no thicker than a hair, and rests in your palm, warm. You don't feel the cold again until breakfast. Learn whose name it is first You ask about the name instead, and get an hour of history you'll need later. The thread comes for you at dawn, the last in the dome, with the tutor already yawning.
